commits.message:
refactor(daemon): a connection runs over any stream, and the net server only hands it a socket (candybar-testing-0x6u.spa) (#521)

* refactor(daemon): a connection runs over any stream, and the net server only hands it a socket (candybar-testing-0x6u.spa)

The request backstop, a half-close, a hang-up, the exit a reply carries and a subscriber's frames lived in server.ts, private to the process shell. They move as they stood to connection.ts, over a Duplex, so a jest worker drives them with no socket.

The connection now states its own half-close rule instead of leaving it to the listener's option, which any other stream would have to repeat. It reaches the exit through the funnel the daemon was built with, so a harness stands in for one exit, not two.

* fix(daemon): an exit a reply carries survives whoever answered first (candybar-testing-0x6u.spa)

A request read after the backstop answered it dropped its exit, because the first responder owned the flush and the late reply only logged. An exit is the request's work, which the backstop does not abandon, so every reply's exit now waits on the one flush, and a subscription, which has none to wait on, lets it through. The connection also states what it needs of a stream: a vanished peer destroys it.

The in-worker cases took the first answer of a cold daemon under the real 200 ms backstop, so a loaded runner read TIMEOUT as a failure. They ask again as a client does, and name what came back. The clock case reads the render event, which an answered backstop does not abandon, from a state dir of its own, because another run's teardown sweeps a lease-less one.

* fix(daemon): an exit stays with its own reply (candybar-testing-0x6u.spa)

A request exits only once its own response has flushed, so its client sees the diagnostic. Exiting on another responder's flush broke that, and on a subscription exited with nothing flushed. So a beaten reply's exit goes unsent with it, loudly, and the client told TIMEOUT asks again. The comment calling this path unreachable was the wrong part: a busy daemon reads a request the backstop has already answered.

The memory line saying no timer stays armed after a close now carves out a connection, which the daemon holds no list of.

* docs(daemon): the connection's comments say what holds of it (candybar-testing-0x6u.spa)

A stream also owes the connection Buffer chunks, a client told TIMEOUT asks again only if it runs on a tick, a subscriber has no backstop to end it after a close, and the pointers to moved code name where it lives now.

feat(carousel): the standard control names the setting it changes, not its value (brandon-menus-sjhy.vxr)

{{ carousel "apply" "open" "label" }} draws ◀ label ▶. The label is required, the neighbour ring and the themeSwitcher segment are gone, and a value outside the domain counts as the first member.
feat(site): the live bar's font size is a slider
feat(site): the live bar's font size is a control, and starts larger
feat(site): site:dev serves the live bar and reloads it on every rebuild
